attributes.action: more support for children in school with mental health
attributes.additional_details: Every child deserves early mental-health support at school. As a parent, I experienced how difficult it was to get my child the right help and had to fight for support. Schools need better training, early identification and clear access to professional support, so children are helped before their mental health reaches crisis point. No parent should have to fight alone for their child to be heard, understood and supported. Early support can change a child's future.
attributes.background: Require all state-funded primary and secondary schools in England to meet a national minimum standard for pupil mental-health support, including early identification of mental-health needs, appropriate staff training, and clear pathways to timely professional support.

rejection.details:
We don't know exactly what you are calling for because there is already statutory guidance for schools which includes mental health & which mentions at least some of things you mention: 

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/keeping-children-safe-in-education--2

We do have some petitions open on related subjects which you may wish to look at and possibly sign: 

Mandate Mental Health Training for All School Staff Who Work With Children
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/752343

Mandate Social, Emotional, and Mental Health informed school behaviour policies
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/777076

Introduce a Mental Health Duty Law
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/770313

Mandate all schools in England to have an SLT member trained for mental health
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/776281

Schools to allow absence exceptions for students with mental health struggles
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759092

Add mental health therapy training to school curriculum
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/758393

Require all schools to carry out autism, ADHD & dyslexia testing
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/766238
